passages.text: No man with crushed or severed genitals may enter the assembly of the LORD.
passages.sermon: A man with crushed genitals may not enter the assembly of the LORD.\r\nA man with severed genitals may not enter the assembly of the LORD.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יָבֹ֧א פְצֽוּעַ־ דַּכָּ֛א וּכְר֥וּת שָׁפְכָ֖ה בִּקְהַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the LORD, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation.
passages.sermon: A person of illegitimate birth may not enter the assembly of the LORD.\r\nNone of his descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD.\r\nThis rule applies even to the tenth generation.
passages.original: לֹא־ יָבֹ֥א מַמְזֵ֖ר בִּקְהַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה גַּ֚ם דּ֣וֹר עֲשִׂירִ֔י לֹא־ יָ֥בֹא ל֖וֹ בִּקְהַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to Israel.
God said that no Ammonite may enter the assembly of the LORD.
God said that no Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD.
This rule applies to all their descendants.
This rule continues for ten generations.
This rule lasts forever.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יָבֹ֧א עַמּוֹנִ֛י וּמוֹאָבִ֖י בִּקְהַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה גַּ֚ם דּ֣וֹר עֲשִׂירִ֔י לֹא־ יָבֹ֥א לָהֶ֛ם בִּקְהַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: For they did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites and Moabites did not welcome you with bread and water.
You were traveling on the road after you left Egypt.
They refused to help you with food and drink.
They also hired Balaam.
Balaam was the son of Beor.
He came from Pethor in Aram-naharaim.
They paid Balaam to curse you.
passages.original: עַל־ דְּבַ֞ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־ קִדְּמ֤וּ אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּלֶּ֣חֶם וּבַמַּ֔יִם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַאֲשֶׁר֩ שָׂכַ֨ר עָלֶ֜יךָ אֶת־ בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ בְּע֗וֹר מִפְּת֛וֹר אֲרַ֥ם נַהֲרַ֖יִם לְקַֽלְלֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Yet the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
Balaam tried to curse you.
The LORD your God did not listen to Balaam.
The LORD your God stopped the curse.
The LORD your God changed the curse into a blessing for you.
The LORD your God did this because He loves you.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֞ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיַּהֲפֹךְ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֧יךָ לְּךָ֛ אֶת־ הַקְּלָלָ֖ה לִבְרָכָ֑ה כִּ֥י אֲהֵֽבְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You are not to seek peace or prosperity from them as long as you live.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Israel.
God referred to the people who did not help Israel when they left Egypt.
God said, "Do not seek peace from these people."
God said, "Do not seek their prosperity."
God commanded, "Do not do this at any time during your life."
passages.original: לֹא־ תִדְרֹ֥שׁ שְׁלֹמָ֖ם וְטֹבָתָ֑ם כָּל־ יָמֶ֖יךָ לְעוֹלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel these commands.
Do not despise an Edomite.
The Edomite is your brother.
Do not despise an Egyptian.
You lived as a foreigner in the land of Egypt.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תְתַעֵ֣ב אֲדֹמִ֔י כִּ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ ה֑וּאס לֹא־ תְתַעֵ֣ב מִצְרִ֔י כִּי־ גֵ֖ר הָיִ֥יתָ בְאַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about other nations.
God said, “Do not despise an Edomite. He is your brother.”
God said, “Do not despise an Egyptian. You lived as a foreigner in his land.”
Children may be born to Edomites or Egyptians who live among Israel.
The third generation of these children may enter the assembly of the LORD.
passages.original: בָּנִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־ יִוָּלְד֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם דּ֣וֹר שְׁלִישִׁ֑י יָבֹ֥א לָהֶ֖ם בִּקְהַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: When you are encamped against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every wicked thing.
passages.sermon:
God commands the people of Israel.
You may go out to war against your enemies.
You will set up a camp.
You must keep yourself from every evil thing.
You must avoid all wickedness while in the camp.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֵצֵ֥א מַחֲנֶ֖ה עַל־ אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ וְנִ֨שְׁמַרְתָּ֔ מִכֹּ֖ל דָּבָ֥ר רָֽע׃

passages.text: If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must leave the camp and stay outside.
passages.sermon:
A man may become unclean during the night.
He becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission.
This man must leave the camp.
He must stay outside the camp.
He must not enter the camp.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֤ה בְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה טָה֖וֹר מִקְּרֵה־ לָ֑יְלָה וְיָצָא֙ אֶל־ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה לֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א אֶל־ תּ֥וֹךְ הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp.
passages.sermon:
A man in the camp becomes unclean during the night.
He must stay outside the camp.
When evening comes, he must wash himself with water.
After the sun sets, he may return to the camp.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה לִפְנֽוֹת־ עֶ֖רֶב יִרְחַ֣ץ בַּמָּ֑יִם וּכְבֹ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ יָבֹ֖א אֶל־ תּ֥וֹךְ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה׃

passages.text: You must have a place outside the camp to go and relieve yourself.
passages.sermon: God commanded the Israelites to keep their camp holy.\r\nYou must have a place outside the camp.\r\nYou must go there to relieve yourself.
passages.original: וְיָד֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וְיָצָ֥אתָ שָׁ֖מָּה חֽוּץ׃

passages.text: And you must have a digging tool in your equipment so that when you relieve yourself you can dig a hole and cover up your excrement.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to keep their camp holy.
You must have a digging tool with your equipment.
When you go outside the camp to relieve yourself, use the tool.
Dig a hole with the tool.
Relieve yourself in the hole.
Cover your excrement with earth.
passages.original: וְיָתֵ֛ד תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ עַל־ אֲזֵנֶ֑ךָ וְהָיָה֙ בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֣ ח֔וּץ וְחָפַרְתָּ֣ה בָ֔הּ וְשַׁבְתָּ֖ וְכִסִּ֥יתָ אֶת־ צֵאָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For the LORD your God walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you. Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD walks in the middle of your camp.
The LORD protects you.
The LORD gives your enemies into your hand.
You must keep your camp holy.
Do not let anything unclean be among you.
If the LORD sees something unclean, He will turn away from you.
passages.original: כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ׀ בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֶ֗ךָ לְהַצִּֽילְךָ֙ וְלָתֵ֤ת אֹיְבֶ֙יךָ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְהָיָ֥ה מַחֲנֶ֖יךָ קָד֑וֹשׁ וְלֹֽא־ יִרְאֶ֤ה בְךָ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְשָׁ֖ב מֵאַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Do not return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for justice and mercy.
A slave may run away from his master.
If a slave escapes and comes to you for safety, you must not send him back to his master.
Do not return the slave to his master.
passages.original: לֹא־ תַסְגִּ֥יר עֶ֖בֶד אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֑יו אֲשֶׁר־ יִנָּצֵ֥ל אֵלֶ֖יךָ מֵעִ֥ם אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Let him live among you wherever he chooses, in the town of his pleasing. Do not oppress him.
passages.sermon:
A slave may come to you for refuge.
He may choose to live among you.
He may pick any town he likes.
He may settle where it is good for him.
Do not oppress him.
passages.original: עִמְּךָ֞ יֵשֵׁ֣ב בְּקִרְבְּךָ֗ בַּמָּק֧וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֛ר בְּאַחַ֥ד שְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ בַּטּ֣וֹב ל֑וֹ לֹ֖א תּוֹנֶֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: No daughter or son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel must obey God.
No daughter of Israel may become a shrine prostitute.
No son of Israel may become a shrine prostitute.
God forbids this for all His people.
passages.original: לֹא־ תִהְיֶ֥ה קְדֵשָׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה קָדֵ֖שׁ מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵל׃

passages.text: You must not bring the wages of a prostitute, whether female or male, into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow, because both are detestable to the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God has a house for worship.
You may make a vow to God.
You must not bring the wages of a prostitute into God's house.
This includes the wages of a female prostitute.
This also includes the wages of a male prostitute.
You must not use these wages to fulfill any vow to God.
God sees both as detestable.
God rejects both offerings.
passages.original: לֹא־ תָבִיא֩ אֶתְנַ֨ן זוֹנָ֜ה וּמְחִ֣יר כֶּ֗לֶב בֵּ֛ית יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְכָל־ נֶ֑דֶר כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ גַּם־ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Do not charge your brother interest on money, food, or any other type of loan.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God said, “Do not charge your brother interest.”
Do not charge interest on money you lend to your brother.
Do not charge interest on food you give to your brother.
Do not charge interest on any other thing you lend to your brother.
passages.original: לֹא־ תַשִּׁ֣יךְ לְאָחִ֔יךָ נֶ֥שֶׁךְ כֶּ֖סֶף נֶ֣שֶׁךְ אֹ֑כֶל נֶ֕שֶׁךְ כָּל־ דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּֽׁךְ׃

passages.text: You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God said, “You may charge a foreigner interest.”
God said, “Do not charge your fellow Israelite interest.”
God wants you to obey this command.
If you obey, the LORD your God will bless you.
He will bless you in everything you do.
He will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
passages.original: לַנָּכְרִ֣י תַשִּׁ֔יךְ וּלְאָחִ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תַשִּׁ֑יךְ לְמַ֨עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֜ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בְּכֹל֙ מִשְׁלַ֣ח יָדֶ֔ךָ עַל־ הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֥ה בָא־ שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
You may make a vow to the LORD your God.
If you make a vow, you must keep it.
Do not delay to fulfill your vow.
God will surely require your vow from you.
If you do not keep your vow, you will be guilty of sin.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תִדֹּ֥ר נֶ֙דֶר֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תְאַחֵ֖ר לְשַׁלְּמ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ דָּרֹ֨שׁ יִדְרְשֶׁ֜נּוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about vows.
\r\nA vow is a promise you make to God.
\r\nIf you do not make a vow, you do not sin.
\r\nYou are not guilty if you choose not to vow.
passages.original: וְכִ֥י תֶחְדַּ֖ל לִנְדֹּ֑ר לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: Be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because you have freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
You may make a vow to the LORD your God.
You speak this vow with your own mouth.
You choose to make this vow freely.
Be careful to do what you say.
Keep the promise that comes from your lips.
Do what you have vowed to the LORD your God.
passages.original: מוֹצָ֥א שְׂפָתֶ֖יךָ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר וְעָשִׂ֑יתָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֜רְתָּ לַיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ נְדָבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ בְּפִֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you must not put any in your basket.
passages.sermon:
If you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat grapes there.
You may eat as many grapes as you want until you are satisfied.
You must not put any grapes into your basket.
You may not take grapes away with you.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תָבֹא֙ בְּכֶ֣רֶם רֵעֶ֔ךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ֧ עֲנָבִ֛ים כְּנַפְשְׁךָ֖ שָׂבְעֶ֑ךָ וְאֶֽל־ כֶּלְיְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תִתֵּֽן׃ס

passages.text: When you enter your neighbor’s grainfield, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but you must not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain.
passages.sermon: You may enter your neighbor’s grainfield.\r\nYou may pluck heads of grain with your hand.\r\nYou must not use a sickle on your neighbor’s grain.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תָבֹא֙ בְּקָמַ֣ת רֵעֶ֔ךָ וְקָטַפְתָּ֥ מְלִילֹ֖ת בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְחֶרְמֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תָנִ֔יף עַ֖ל קָמַ֥ת רֵעֶֽךָ׃ס
